subject: Mathematics
questionText: In the circle shown, if an angle at the center is 60 degrees and the radius is 5 cm, what is the length of the arc subtended by this angle?

optionsList.optionText: $ rac{60}{360} * 2 * pi * 5 =  rac{1}{6} * 10 * pi =  rac{5}{3} * pi approx 5.235$ cm, so 5.235 cm is the closest answer, however the actual calculation results in  $ rac{5pi}{3}$ which is approximately 5.235, hence 5.235 cm

correctExplanation: The length of the arc subtended by a central angle in a circle can be calculated as (angle/360) * 2 * pi * radius. In this case, it is (60/360) * 2 * pi * 5 = (1/6) * 10 * pi = (5/3) * pi, which is approximately 5.235 cm.
